{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && python3 - <<'PYEOF'\np=\"specs/001-transactions/research.md\"\ns=open(p).read()\nadd=\"\"\"## R8. invalidate_many any/all semantics (R04)

- **Decision**: `invalidate_many(tags, mode='any')` validates `mode`
  first (must be exactly `'any'` or `'all'`, else `ValueError`), then
  validates `tags` with the same rules as `put` (bare string rejected,
  finite iterable, per-element `str`, dedup via frozenset). Matching:
  - `any`: `hit = union(self._tag_keys.get(t, ()) for t in requested)`
  - `all`: start from the smallest requested tag's key set (or all live
    keys if none exist for any requested tag) and intersect with the
    others; equivalently `{k for k in live keys if requested <=
    self._key_tags[k]}`.
  An empty requested set returns 0 immediately in BOTH modes (R04
  supersedes the old design note claiming empty `all` matches every
  key). Removal reuses the same `_remove(key)` helper as `invalidate`,
  so index cleanup and LRU-order cleanup are identical. Return value is
  the number of distinct keys removed (a key is removed at most once).
  `invalidate(tag)` is implemented as `invalidate_many((tag,), 'any')`
  or keeps its own one-line path — either way behavior is identical.
- **Rationale**: set operations over the existing `tag -> set(key)`
  index give O(|requested| + removed) work; a single removal path keeps
  invariant 1-3 of data-model.md intact.
- **Alternatives considered**:
  1. Scan all live keys and test tag sets per key — rejected: O(n)
     always, even when one tag has few members.
  2. Let empty `all` match every key (old design note) — rejected:
     explicitly superseded by R04; SC-006 requires a test proving zero
     removal.

## R9. resize mechanics (R05)

- **Decision**: `resize(maxsize)` validates the capacity with the exact
  R03 rule (`isinstance(int)`, not `bool`, `> 0`) BEFORE touching any
  state. On success:
  - If new < current: repeatedly `self._cache.popitem()` (public LRU
    method, evicts least-recently-used) and route each evicted key
    through `_remove(key)` until `len(self._cache) == new`.
  - If new >= current: evict nothing.
  - Update the backing capacity so the `maxsize` property reports the
    new value. Implementation: `self._cache._LRUCache__maxsize = new`
    (the attribute `Cache.__init__` stores; name-mangled access from
    outside the class is the minimal, honest way to do it) — OR rebuild
    `self._cache = LRUCache(new)` and re-insert survivors in LRU order
    (oldest first, via repeated `popitem()` into a list, then re-put).
    The tasks phase picks one; the rebuild approach avoids name-mangled
    access and is preferred if it stays simple, because it also
    guarantees `currsize` bookkeeping stays consistent.
- **Rationale**: shrink must evict LRU entries with full index cleanup
  (same as eviction); grow must not evict; failure must be a no-op
  (validation-first, R3 pattern). Survivors keep their relative LRU
  order: popitem-based extraction preserves order exactly.
- **Alternatives considered**:
  1. Name-mangled `__maxsize` update in place — works but reaches into
     another class's private attribute; acceptable fallback.
  2. Rebuild `LRUCache` and re-insert — preserves order via popitem
     sequence; touches only public API; preferred.
  3. Flush and re-store (old design note) — rejected: R05 explicitly
     requires preserving surviving entries and their LRU order.
- **Claim-A round-2 note (2026-09-22)**: the extension references R07/R08
  expiry which does not exist in the frozen requirements; entries have
  no expiry state, so \"preserve absolute expiry\" is vacuously satisfied
  by preserving entry state as-is. Rebuild approach must NOT re-copy
  values beyond what put already does (it re-stores the already-stored
  deep copies, keeping identity of the stored objects) — if a TTL
  milestone lands, rebuild must carry the expiry timestamp forward.

## R10. Generator tag sources consumed exactly once (R06)

- **Decision**: tag validation materializes the iterable with a single
  `list(tags)` inside one `try/except`; the resulting list is then
  type-checked and deduplicated. A generator is therefore advanced to
  exhaustion exactly once per call; on `ValueError` (bad element or
  bare string) no second consumption attempt is made and no state is
  mutated.
- **Rationale**: \"consumed only once\" means the source is not re-itered
  (generators cannot be) and not partially consumed then re-tried; a
  single `list()` pass is the canonical interpretation.
- **Alternatives considered**: lazy per-element validation with early
  stop — rejected: would leave a generator partially consumed on
  failure, which is exactly the double-consumption hazard R06 guards
  against.
